entries.test: Contemporaneous trends in generative AI investment, valuations and investor demand would show whether the boom was contracting in July 2024.
entries.note: The metaphor has a plain economic reading in context.

entries.test: Public estimates of cumulative AI investment, carrying costs and required returns would show whether longer delays increase the earnings needed to recoup investment.
entries.note: The surrounding discussion supplies an investment-return interpretation.
The capability assertion is testable separately, but the extracted proposition includes an explicitly tentative causal explanation.
Difficulty seeing a route forward does not assert that advancement is unlikely. The source describes an unclear prospect rather than a definite outcome.
“Has the potential” asserts a possibility.

entries.test: Published model scaling results and training costs would show whether equal performance improvements require exponentially increasing expenditure.
Documented deployments showing generative AI solving substantive robotics or supply-chain problems would contradict the forecast.

entries.note: “Might” makes the operational failure a possibility.

entries.test: Public deployment studies available in July 2024 would establish the range of tasks generative AI completed without human performance of those tasks.
Public operating results for the discussed restaurant ordering systems would show whether they could replace the intended workers' full jobs.
entries.note: The source discusses restaurant automation; the normalization broadens this to generative AI products generally.

entries.test: Workplace deployment and freelance-market evidence would show whether generative AI replaced discrete paid tasks more successfully than entire jobs.

entries.note: The central comparison of workers' value has no specified shared standard. The employment-pressure component could be checked separately.

entries.test: Public evaluations of dataset-trained systems handling client feedback, revisions and unforeseen creative requirements would test the asserted inability.
entries.note: The preceding paragraph supplies concrete behaviors for the capability claim.
The source explicitly conditions its “very unlikely” prediction on the training approach.

entries.test: Public financial disclosures and customer studies would show whether generative AI produced additional revenue for users and earnings for providers.
July 2024 employment records, documented workflows and financial results would show whether generative AI had created jobs, new working methods or monetary gains.

entries.note: Calling Covello optimistic evaluates his outlook without committing to an alternative date or outcome.

entries.test: Contemporaneous product adoption, revenue, employment and productivity evidence would test the claimed absence of economic and industrial effects.
Public utility capacity studies and AI electricity-demand projections would show whether meeting AI demand requires rebuilding the entire US grid.
entries.note: “Totally” is a sweeping infrastructure claim that can be assessed.
The sarcastic phrasing conveys a recommendation about who should pay.

entries.test: Public hiring and employment records from the 18 months before July 2024 would show whether generative AI created new jobs.
Historical costs for comparable AI workloads and publicly documented efficiency improvements through July 2024 would test the claimed lack of cost reductions and a route to further reductions.
entries.note: The qualified assessment of a path forward accompanies a firm historical cost claim.

entries.test: Public paid adoption, customer retention and sales-growth evidence would show whether substantial demand or a demonstrated route to it existed in July 2024.
Dated technical records or subsequent disclosures of OpenAI's July 2024 internal systems would show whether it possessed an unreleased breakthrough.
entries.note: An unreleased product can later be documented publicly; secrecy alone does not make the claim uncheckable.
The normalization applies Altman's explicit horizon to all three companies and replaces “makes me eat crow” with an investment criterion. “Makes all of this worth it” has no agreed standard.

entries.test: Public capability evaluations before and after July 2024 would show whether generative AI had reached a plateau in substantive capabilities.
entries.note: The following sentence identifies capabilities as the relevant sense of “peaking.”

entries.test: Demonstrated substantive capabilities beyond July 2024 systems, excluding speed increases and new input formats alone, would contradict the forecast.
Contemporaneous measurements of compute, energy and cost per comparable-quality output would show whether generative AI efficiency was materially improving.

entries.note: The assertion concerns what increased speed can cause. Sentience, intelligence and consciousness are combined without an agreed public test.

entries.test: A publicly demonstrated generative AI system reliably performing the broad range of intellectual tasks of a general human-level assistant would contradict the forecast.
entries.note: The surrounding Jarvis example gives the broad capability claim a practical reading.
The quotation marks and contrast with mathematical processing invoke an unspecified notion of genuine understanding. Readers could disagree despite identical behavioral evidence.
The sweeping accusation identifies neither a specific representation nor a concrete standard for the hyped intelligence.

entries.test: Public labor-market studies establishing material changes in employment, occupations or hiring attributable to generative AI would contradict the forecast.
Public pricing histories and financial disclosures would show whether these providers raise prices or experience financial collapse because their services cannot cover costs.
entries.note: “I believe” introduces a firm “will have to” prediction here.
Whether the benefits justify the resource demands is a judgment of worth.

entries.test: Google's emissions reports, disclosed emissions drivers and independent search-quality evaluations would test the numerical increase and its asserted connection to AI.
entries.note: The normalization attributes the entire 48% increase to AI more explicitly than the source does.

entries.test: Public shareholder actions, market reactions and investment disclosures during an AI downturn would show whether investor punishment of a major provider contributed to the collapse.
entries.note: The central prediction is firm; only the identity of the punished provider is probabilistic.

entries.test: Public records of an AI-sector collapse would show whether successive setbacks culminated in a major destabilizing event.
entries.note: A major company's collapse is offered as an example of the culminating event, not a required outcome.

entries.test: Public reporting would establish either a scare prompting a VC to push an AI startup into a sale or a major AI company's sudden collapse.
entries.note: The normalization omits the triggering scare and would count an ordinary investor-directed sale.

entries.test: Public financial results and business plans would show whether OpenAI and Anthropic could reach profitability through their existing generative AI businesses.
entries.note: The source denies a path to profitability and describes speculative spending; it does not affirm a breakthrough route as an exception.

entries.test: Public funding and compute agreements, together with product-development records, would show whether withdrawal of cloud subsidies forces the companies to stop iterating on LLMs.

entries.note: “It is unclear how” expresses uncertainty about a survival route, not a definite conditional failure prediction.

entries.test: Public financial disclosures and business projections as of July 2024 would show cash burn and whether a credible route to positive returns existed.
Public financial results and controlled studies of probabilistic generation would test the asserted losses, operating constraints and causal capability limits.
entries.note: The explicit explanation of limitations makes causal the better classification.

entries.test: Documented model capabilities and deployed applications across the 18 months before July 2024 would show whether substantive new uses emerged.

entries.note: The overall proposition judges whether AI justifies its costs and existence. The narrower assertion that costs are not falling is separately testable.

entries.test: Public adoption, retention and commercial results, together with announced products in July 2024, would show whether a compelling mass-demand application existed or was emerging.
entries.note: “On the horizon” describes the visible pipeline rather than asserting that no such application will ever exist.
“Shockwaves” specifies no outcome, magnitude or shared criterion for industry disruption.
“Disgraceful waste” is a judgment of worth.
